findings.comment: Retaining wall detail sheets (38-39) show structural sections and dimensions but lack any section view exhibits showing clearance dimensions from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of retaining wall faces where overhead electric facilities exist adjacent to wall locations.

findings.comment: Two main site entrances (Type II Driveways) cross the overhead electric line on the southern boundary. No mid-span clearance verification survey data from registered surveyor is provided.
applicableAreas: Driveways crossing or located beneath overhead electric lines on southern property boundary

findings.comment: Driveways are proposed on the site plan, and overhead electric lines exist. However, no vertical clearance dimension annotations are provided showing the clearance from the lowest point of the overhead facilities to finished driveway grades. Code requires 16 feet minimum (parking without truck traffic) or 18 feet (areas with truck traffic). Mid-span clearance verification from registered surveyor is not provided.
applicableAreas: Driveways and parking areas potentially beneath or adjacent to overhead electric facilities

findings.comment: Driveways are shown on the site plan in proximity to overhead electric facilities. Minimum 16-foot vertical clearance (parking without truck traffic) or 18-foot vertical clearance (areas with truck traffic) is required, but no vertical clearance dimensions are provided. Grading plan shows finished floor elevations but not vertical clearance from driveways to the lowest point of overhead facilities.
applicableAreas: Driveways adjacent to or beneath overhead distribution line routing

findings.comment: The site plan shows overhead electric facilities but provides NO clearance dimensions at all on any sheet. Where clearances should be annotated from the outside conductor to building edges, driveways, or other site features per UCM § 1.10.3 and the grouping guidance (dimensions must originate from outer conductor, not pole centerline), NO DIMENSIONS are provided. This is a fundamental documentation failure preventing any clearance verification.
applicableAreas: All overhead electric facilities on site - eastern and southern boundaries where OHE lines are shown

findings.comment: Overhead electric lines and utility poles are shown on the site plan, but NO clearance dimensions are annotated on any sheets (site plan, grading plan, or other exhibits). When clearance dimensions are eventually provided, they must be measured from the outside conductor, not from pole centerline or pole structure. Code requires dimensions originating from conductor location.
applicableAreas: All site features and overhead electric facilities where clearances apply

findings.comment: No clearance dimensions are shown on any plan sheets. The site plan and landscape plan identify the overhead electric (OHE) line but provide zero dimension annotations measuring clearances from the outside conductor to any site features. The grouping regulatory overview explicitly warns against 'Clearances measured from pole instead of conductor: Dimension annotations read "10'-0" from pole" instead of "15'-0" from outside conductor"; conductor may be several feet offset from pole center on three-phase installations.' This project provides no dimensions at all.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric line and all site features in proximity

findings.comment: Site plan shows two main driveways crossing overhead electric lines on southern boundary with no surveyed conductor elevation data or mid-span clearance documentation provided. Given the absence of any vertical clearance dimensions and the presence of OHE lines crossing driveways, a registered surveyor's mid-span clearance verification is required but not provided. UCM § 1.10.3 explicitly requires this documentation when vertical clearances may not meet minimums.
applicableAreas: Driveways and buildings relative to overhead electric facilities where vertical clearances appear marginal

findings.comment: No registered surveyor data showing pole locations and mid-span clearances is provided in the site plan package. Code requires surveyor-certified mid-span clearance verification when existing overhead facilities may not meet minimum vertical clearance requirements (7.5-foot sky-to-ground, 16-18 feet for driveways). Without this data, vertical clearances cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All site features where overhead facilities may not meet minimum vertical clearance requirements

findings.comment: Overhead electric line is present on the southern boundary with buildings and driveways nearby. The clearances from site features to the overhead line appear marginal based on the site plan visual layout, but no registered surveyor data is provided showing pole locations and mid-span clearances. Without surveyed elevation data, compliance with vertical clearance requirements cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Buildings 7 and 8 adjacent to southern overhead line; all driveways in proximity

findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows proposed tree plantings but does not verify that trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors are from Utility Compatible Shade Trees list (ECM Appendix F, UC column), nor does it measure lateral distances from tree locations to conductors. Required clearance distances are not annotated.
applicableAreas: Tree planting locations on landscape plan, particularly trees near overhead electric lines on property boundaries

findings.comment: Trees are proposed on the landscape plan (Sheet 31) within what appears to be 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors based on visual spacing and symbol overlap. However, the specific species of these proposed trees are not identified on the landscape plan. Tree species verification against ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible trees list (generally mature height ≤20 feet) cannot be performed without this information.
applicableAreas: Landscape areas along southern and western property boundaries adjacent to overhead distribution conductors

findings.comment: Landscape plan shows mitigation trees (designated 'M') located near the overhead electric (OHE) line on the southern boundary. No clearance verification or species identification is provided for trees within the 10-foot lateral distance requirement from overhead distribution conductors.
applicableAreas: Landscape area near overhead distribution line along southern boundary

findings.comment: Required note regarding 48-hour notification to Austin Energy before work near high-voltage overhead lines is NOT included on the cover sheet or general notes. The cover sheet (Sheet 1) lacks this required note.
applicableAreas: Cover sheet and general notes where required notification requirement should be stated

findings.comment: Overhead electric lines exist on site and construction activities are proposed. However, no note is provided on the cover sheet or general notes requiring that the owner/contractor notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines, as required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.
applicableAreas: Cover sheet and general notes for construction phase notifications

findings.comment: The general notes on Sheet 3 do not include a required note stating that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines, as required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003. While Sheet 3 contains extensive Austin Energy requirements and Electric Transmission Notes, the specific 48-hour notification requirement for overhead distribution lines is not explicitly stated as a general note.
applicableAreas: Overall site with overhead electric facilities

findings.comment: Trees are proposed within 15 feet of overhead electric distribution lines (some as close as 3-5 feet), but species are not identified at these locations on the landscape plan, making it impossible to verify utility compatibility. Western boundary overhead electric line

findings.comment: Wastewater line routing is shown on utility plans and electrical plan but horizontal clearance distances between transformer pads and wastewater service lines are not dimensioned. Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Storm drain line routes are shown but clearance dimensions to transformer pads are not provided. Applicant must provide dimensioned utility coordination plan showing minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from storm drain lines to all transformer pad edges.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Storm drain line routing is shown on grading and drainage plans (Sheet 12) and electrical plan (Sheet 21) but horizontal clearance distances between transformer pads and storm drain lines are not dimensioned. Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Sheet 21 shows transformer pads and underground utility lines, but no dimension lines measure the 12-inch minimum horizontal and vertical clearance from transformer pads to other underground utilities. Compliance with UCM § 1.10.5.A separation requirements cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: all transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Utility line routing is shown in plan view but specific horizontal and vertical clearance dimensions are not provided. applicableAreas: transformer pad and underground electrical routing

findings.comment: Utility routing (electrical, water, wastewater, storm drain, telephone) is shown on various plan sheets but the horizontal and vertical clearance distances between transformer pads and other underground utilities are not dimensioned. findings.comment: Plat and Site Plans show easement callouts (drainage, water, wastewater, electrical). No explicit notation confirms whether any transformer pad is located within prohibited easements (drainage, water, sewer, or electrical easements under overhead lines). No Austin Energy Design written approval for pad placement in easements is documented.
codeCitations: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 4 (property requirement); easement-specific regulations
applicableAreas: all transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Transformer pad locations relative to easement boundaries are not clearly dimensioned or verified. Facts.md documents two critical undepicted easements in NE area that must be added to site plan before approval. Applicant must: (1) clearly show all easement boundaries on electrical plan with transformer locations dimensioned relative to easement edges; (2) confirm no transformer pads are located in drainage, water, sewer, or electrical easements, or provide Austin Energy Design written approval for any proposed locations; (3) add missing greenbelt access easement and drainage easement to site plan exhibits.
applicableAreas: all transformer pad locations relative to documented and undocumented easements

findings.comment: Transformer pads must not be located in prohibited easements (drainage, water, sewer, or electrical easements under overhead lines) without written Austin Energy Design approval. Transformer pad locations are not dimensioned relative to the documented easements. Facts.md identifies that two critical easements (Instruments 2010070731 and 2011021137) are not depicted on the site plan. Additional plat-dedicated easements (Cortez Heights and Trico Subdivision easements) are also not verified on the submitted site plan.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Easement callouts appear on plat and site plan boundary areas (drainage, water, electrical), but no specific transformer pad easement callouts or dimensions are shown on the electrical plan. Easement width adequate for Austin Energy accessibility requirements cannot be verified from submitted evidence.
codeCitations: UCM § 1.10.3 (additional clearance and access easements may be required)
applicableAreas: all transformer pad locations

findings.comment: No transformer easements are shown on any submitted plan sheet. Applicant must provide easement exhibit showing transformer easements of adequate width around all four transformer pad locations. Submit Austin Energy Design specifications for required easement width and coordinate with AE Design business unit for appropriate easement configuration and recording requirements.
applicableAreas: all four transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Transformer easements are not shown on the electrical or site plans. The UCM § 1.10.3 and associated regulations require transformer easements around pads for Austin Energy Design accessibility and maintenance, with width determined by AE Design on a project-specific basis. No easement boundaries, widths, or AE Design approval documentation are provided in the submitted plans.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Sheet 21 shows transformer pads and meter locations connected by blue electrical lines, but no dimension lines or property line callouts confirm that the electrical routing from each transformer pad to its corresponding meter is 100% on private property and does not cross property lines or right-of-way areas.
applicableAreas: electrical service routing from all transformer pads to meters

findings.comment: Complete electrical routing from transformers to service meters is not clearly shown or verified to be 100% on private property. Applicant must provide detailed electrical routing plan with property boundary overlay showing the complete path from each transformer pad to its corresponding building service meter, confirming all routing remains on private property and outside public right-of-way and utility easements.
applicableAreas: electrical routing from all transformer pads to building service meters

findings.comment: Electrical routing from transformer pads to meters must be 100% on private property. The routing is shown on the electrical plan but routing paths are not dimensioned or explicitly labeled to confirm they do not cross right-of-way, easements, or other properties.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Sheet 21 shows four transformer pad locations but provides no dimensions (length x width). No reference callouts or detail reference bubbles direct readers to Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets. No specification of service type (single-phase or three-phase) is provided. Required transformer pad dimensions and AE Design detail references matching the specified service type are not documented.
codeCitations: UCM § 1.18.0 (obtain transformer pad detail from AE Design)
applicableAreas: all transformer pad locations (4 pads identified)

findings.comment: No transformer pad dimensions are shown on any submitted plan or detail sheet, and no Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets are included. Applicant must obtain from Austin Energy Design the transformer pad detail sheets corresponding to the specified service type (single-phase or three-phase) and provide: (1) dimensioned pad configuration details; (2) equipment specifications including transformer ratings and pad dimensions; (3) confirmation of compliance with AE Design requirements; (4) reference callouts on electrical plan sheet 21 to applicable AE Design standard details.
applicableAreas: all four transformer pads

findings.comment: No Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets are provided or referenced. Transformer pad dimensions are not specified on the electrical design plan. The UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.18.0 require that pad dimensions match AE Design-approved specifications for the proposed service type (single-phase or three-phase). Without these details, the adequacy and compliance of pad installation cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Site plan shows transformer pads and parking areas. Specific dimension lines measuring distances from each transformer pad to nearby parking spaces and drive aisles are not provided. No bollard details or protective barrier specifications are shown on the electrical plan or referenced in detail sheets. If any pad is located within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas, required 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal post specifications and spacing cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations (only if within 4 feet of parking or vehicle routes)

findings.comment: West-central transformer pad is positioned between building and parking aisle. No dimensions are provided showing clearance to parking area. No bollards are detailed. Applicant must either: (1) provide dimensioned plan showing transformer pad is more than 4 feet from parking area edge, OR (2) provide AE Design equipment pad detail sheets with 4-inch diameter galvanized rigid metal bollard specifications and site plan showing bollard placement and spacing to allow equipment door opening.
applicableAreas: west-central transformer pad (west of Building 2)

findings.comment: When transformer pads are located within 4 feet of parking areas or vehicle circulation routes, 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal bollards are required per AE Design specifications. No bollard specifications, details, or locations are shown on the electrical or site plans. Whether transformer pads are within the 4-foot threshold of parking cannot be definitively confirmed from the submitted plans.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 1 (near parking area entrance), Transformer Pad 5 (near internal parking/drive area)

findings.comment: No building elevation or section views provided showing building projections (overhangs, balconies, roof details) and their clearances from overhead electric conductors. Clearance verification from both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial envelopes cannot be assessed.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8, specifically evaluating overhangs, awnings, balconies, roof overhangs relative to nearby overhead electric lines

findings.comment: No building elevation sheets or section views are provided showing building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, roofs) in relation to overhead electric conductors. Without these exhibits, the required 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances for projections cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Building projections (overhangs, balconies, roofs)

findings.comment: Buildings maintain setback from property lines where electric easements are recorded, but no surveyed clearance dimensions from outside conductor to building faces are provided to demonstrate both 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances are maintained as permanent requirements per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: Buildings 5-8 relative to electric facilities in right-of-way and easements on eastern and southern boundaries

findings.comment: Overhead electric facilities exist in the Valley View Road right-of-way adjacent to the site. Buildings are proposed adjacent to this ROW, but no clearance dimension annotations demonstrate maintenance of the minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from these ROW facilities.
applicableAreas: Buildings near Valley View Road right-of-way with adjacent overhead electric facilities

findings.comment: Two main site driveways cross or are immediately adjacent to overhead electric utility poles and lines on the southern boundary (visible on Sheet 9 vision analysis). No dimension annotations show 30-foot minimum clearance from driveway edge to pole locations, and no pole relocation notes are provided.
applicableAreas: Driveway locations relative to existing electric utility poles on southern boundary

findings.comment: Existing electric poles are shown on existing conditions survey. Proposed driveways are shown on site plan. However, no dimension annotations demonstrate the horizontal distance from driveway edges to existing poles, and no notes indicate whether poles will be relocated minimum 30 feet from driveway edges.
applicableAreas: Driveways and site features in proximity to existing electric poles

findings.comment: Trash receptacles and enclosure areas are shown on site plan, but no dimension annotations demonstrate that trash areas maintain 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance from overhead electric facilities when trash bins are raised during service.
applicableAreas: Trash enclosure locations relative to overhead electric facilities

findings.comment: Trash enclosure locations are shown on site plan. Overhead electric lines are present. However, no clearance dimension annotations demonstrate that trash enclosures maintain the required 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance considering trash bin raised height during service.
applicableAreas: Trash enclosure and receptacle locations

findings.comment: Electric easements are shown on plat (Sheet 2) and grading plan (Sheet 11) with recorded 5' electric easement dimensions noted. However, the site plan does NOT provide clearance dimension annotations demonstrating that items within electric easements maintain minimum 7.5-foot clearance from outside conductor as required. The grouping regulatory overview explicitly states the absolute prohibition against customer facilities installed 'under or over' distribution facilities, separate from maintaining distance clearances, but clearance dimensions are not provided to verify compliance.
applicableAreas: Electric easement areas on eastern and southern property boundaries where overhead electric lines and distribution facilities exist

findings.comment: Overhead distribution facilities are shown on site plan. While buildings appear positioned away from direct conflict based on visual spacing, the lack of surveyed conductor locations and explicit dimensional evidence means that compliance with the absolute prohibition against installing customer facilities under or over overhead distribution facilities cannot be conclusively verified.
applicableAreas: Buildings, structures, and site features within or beneath existing overhead distribution facilities

findings.comment: Utility tap plans (Sheets 19-20) show water and wastewater connections but do not show water meter locations or service drops with clearance dimension annotations showing 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductor of overhead electric service-drop conductors.
applicableAreas: Water meter location relative to overhead electric service drops

findings.comment: Water meter locations are shown on the electrical design plan (Sheet 21). However, no clearance dimension annotations demonstrate that water meters maintain the minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead electric service-drop conductors.
applicableAreas: Water meter locations relative to overhead electric service drops

findings.comment: Utility tap plans show water line routing but do not provide dimension annotations or clearance notes demonstrating minimum clearance from proposed water lines to overhead electrical distribution facilities shown on site plan.
applicableAreas: Water line routing relative to overhead electric distribution facilities

findings.comment: Water lines are shown on utility plans. Overhead distribution lines are shown on site plan. However, no clearance dimension annotations demonstrate that water lines maintain required clearances from overhead distribution facilities.
applicableAreas: Water line routing beneath or adjacent to overhead electrical distribution facilities

findings.comment: Buildings 5-8 are shown near the eastern property boundary where electric facilities exist in adjacent ROW/easements. No clearance space verification is provided showing that building setbacks allow necessary clearance for electric facility installation and maintenance.
applicableAreas: Buildings 5-8 on eastern property boundary within 5 feet of property line

findings.comment: Building foundations are shown on site plan, some within or near 5-foot distance from property lines where electric facilities may be required in adjacent ROW or property. However, no dimension annotations show the clearance space from property line to building foundation to verify that adequate room exists for necessary electric facility maintenance and access.
applicableAreas: Building foundations within 5 feet of property line

findings.comment: Overhead electric lines cross the property and site driveways on plan view, but the angle of crossing relative to roadway alignment is not annotated or verified. Cannot determine if crossings are perpendicular to driveway centerlines as required.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric line crossing alignment relative to roadway

findings.comment: Overhead electric lines cross Valley View Road at the site property boundary. However, no angle dimension annotation demonstrates that the crossing is oriented at 90-degree angle to the road centerline as required.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric line crossings of Valley View Road

findings.comment: Preliminary electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows meter locations on site but does not provide enlarged meter area details showing clearance from obstructions (fences, walls, landscaping, building projections) that would conflict with meter access, installation, and required 30-inch-wide front space, 36-inch front depth, and 6.5-foot headroom per UCM § 1.10.9.
applicableAreas: Electric meter locations proposed on site

findings.comment: Meter locations are shown on electrical plan (Sheet 21). However, no detailed site plan or meter area enlargement is provided showing working clearances around meter locations. Code requires 30-inch-wide front space, 36-inch front depth, and 6.5-foot headroom per UCM § 1.10.9, free of obstructions including fences, walls, equipment, vegetation, and building projections.
applicableAreas: Electric meter locations and meter equipment clearances

findings.comment: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows at least one down guy wire symbol at bottom-left corner (visible in vision analysis), but site plan and grading plan do not identify all guy wire locations or verify that proposed accessible paths, driveways, and site features do not conflict with guy anchor points. No pole relocation or conversion notes are provided.
applicableAreas: Down guy wire locations from existing overhead electric poles

findings.comment: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows down guy wires (e.g., AT&T pole with guy wire shown). However, proposed site plan does not clearly depict existing down guy wire locations, and there are no notes indicating whether conflicts with proposed accessible paths, driveways, or site features have been identified and resolved through pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting poles.
applicableAreas: Down guy wire locations from existing electric poles

findings.comment: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows at least one down guy wire and anchor, but the plat (Sheet 2) and grading plan do not show dedicated guy anchor easements with the required 10-foot width and 5-foot extension past anchor ground entry point as required by Austin Energy Transmission Engineering Standards.
applicableAreas: Down guy anchor locations from distribution poles on site

findings.comment: Down guy anchors are visible on existing conditions survey (utilities shown with guy wires). However, no down guy anchor easements are depicted on the easement exhibits or site plan. Code requires dedicated easements 10 feet wide extending 5 feet past where down guy enters the ground. Without easement depiction, the requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Down guy anchor points from existing electric poles

findings.comment: Sheet 3 references construction sequence and staging notes. Sheet 5 shows erosion control plan. However, no site logistics plan or construction phasing plan is provided showing construction staging areas, crane swing radius, material storage, or scaffold locations with 10-foot radial clearance verification from energized overhead lines as required by OSHA and UCM § 1.10.2.
applicableAreas: Construction staging areas, equipment operation zones, and work platforms adjacent to overhead electric lines

findings.comment: Overhead electric lines exist on and adjacent to the site. Construction activities are proposed. However, no construction staging plan, site logistics plan, or phasing plan is provided in the submitted site plan package showing construction staging area boundaries, crane swing radius, or material storage locations relative to overhead electric lines. Code requires 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead lines for construction activities.
applicableAreas: Construction staging areas, equipment operation zones, and work platforms

findings.comment: Underground electric lines are shown on the landscape plan (marked as '- E -' on Sheet 31). However, the specific locations of underground electric equipment (pull boxes, vaults, buried transformers, etc.) are not clearly identified on the landscape plan. Without identified equipment locations and without dimensioned clearances, the 5-foot minimum clearance requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Areas where underground electric lines and equipment are located

findings.comment: Underground electric lines and pull boxes are shown on Sheet 21 electrical plan. Landscape plan shows trees throughout site but no clearance measurements documented to verify 5-foot minimum distance from underground equipment.
applicableAreas: Areas along underground electric lines and pull box locations

findings.comment: Underground electric equipment locations are not clearly identified on the landscape plan. Therefore, it cannot be determined which proposed trees fall within the 20-foot proximity zone requiring root barriers. Additionally, no root barrier specifications are shown on the landscape plan or in the landscape notes. Without identified equipment locations and without documented root barrier specifications, compliance cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Areas where trees are proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment

findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) and landscape details (Sheet 37) do not show root barrier specifications. No 4-foot deep root barriers positioned 5 feet from underground equipment are detailed or dimensioned on the landscape plans.
applicableAreas: Areas where trees are proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment

findings.comment: The landscape plan identifies trees only by regulatory category (M, ST, PL, P) without species names. The plant schedule lists species using different symbols with no cross-reference to the landscape plan. A unified plant legend must be provided on the landscape plan identifying each tree location by species name (common and/or scientific) to allow verification of utility compatibility and mature height characteristics near electric facilities.
applicableAreas: All trees proposed on landscape plan (sheets 31)
Trees within 15 feet of overhead electric distribution lines
Trees near pad-mounted equipment

findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) uses generic tree symbols (circles labeled with M, SY, PL, P designations) without species identification. Plant species names are listed separately on Sheet 35 plant schedule but are not identified on the landscape plan drawing itself, preventing verification of species placement relative to electrical infrastructure.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan areas where trees are shown near electric facilities

findings.comment: While the landscape plan does show the OHE utility line and trees in relation to it (both are depicted on Sheet 31), the plan fails to demonstrate compliance because no clearance dimensions are provided between tree trunk centers and the conductor line. Trees shown with canopies overlapping the OHE line position lack any dimensioned clearance verification. Reviewer cannot verify clearance compliance from the presented evidence.
applicableAreas: Southern boundary where OHE line runs parallel to property line
Street yard areas where trees are in proximity to utility facilities

findings.comment: Landscape plan shows both tree symbols and overhead electric (OHE) line on the same drawing but lacks sufficient documentation to verify clearances. Vision analysis identified trees positioned directly on or immediately adjacent to OHE line markings on southern boundary, with no dimensions, callouts, or notes confirming clearance compliance. Cross-reference to electrical plan (Sheet 21) required for clearance verification is not explicitly shown.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan areas showing trees in proximity to overhead electric lines

findings.comment: Site plan shows retaining walls around the property perimeter. Transformer pad locations are shown, but no dimension lines measure clearance distances from any transformer pad to adjacent retaining walls. The 5-foot minimum clearance from retaining walls cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations (only if retaining walls are present and adjacent to pads)

findings.comment: Retaining walls are present on site but clearance distances from transformer pads are not dimensioned. Provide dimensioned plan showing minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pad edges to all retaining wall structures.
applicableAreas: retaining walls on north, east, south site boundaries and detention pond perimeter

findings.comment: The site plan shows building footprints and transformer pad locations, but no vertical elevations or cross-sections are provided for the transformer pad areas showing whether balconies or building overhangs exist above or adjacent to any pad. Additionally, no dimension lines show clearance distances. Compliance cannot be verified from available evidence.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations (only if balconies or overhangs are present above or adjacent)

findings.comment: No cross-section drawings or building elevation details provided showing vertical clearances from transformer pads to building balconies, overhangs, or structures. Provide architectural cross-sections for each transformer location demonstrating minimum 5-foot lateral clearance from balconies/overhangs and confirmation that no structures cover pad areas.
applicableAreas: all transformer pad locations

findings.comment: No building elevation sheets showing window/door/duct locations relative to transformer pads were provided. No dimension lines show clearance distances from pads to windows, doors, or ventilating ducts. Specification of transformer equipment as oil-filled or dry-type was not provided. Compliance with the 12-foot horizontal clearance requirement for oil-filled equipment with inadequate lateral separation cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations (only if windows, doors, or ventilating ducts are present with inadequate separation)

findings.comment: Building elevation drawings are not provided. Applicant must submit: (1) building elevation details showing all windows, doors, and ventilating ducts adjacent to transformer locations; (2) confirmation of oil-filled vs. dry-type equipment; (3) dimensional clearance analysis demonstrating 12-foot horizontal clearance when lateral separation is less than 5 feet or when openings are less than 12 feet from grade.
applicableAreas: all transformer pad locations

findings.comment: No cross-section drawings or elevation views showing whether any transformer pads are located in niches, vaults, or enclosed areas were provided. No documentation of 35-foot vertical clearance inside niche and niche entrance if applicable. Confined space configuration cannot be verified from submitted plans.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations (only if in confined space such as niche, vault, or notched-out building area)

findings.comment: No cross-section drawings are provided showing vertical clearances in areas with building overhangs, enclosed configurations, or notched-out areas adjacent to transformer locations. Provide cross-section drawings for any transformer location adjacent to building elements that might create a confined space configuration requiring 15-foot hot-stick clearance and 35-foot vertical clearance in niche.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Fire Protection Plan shows 3 fire hydrant locations (1 existing, 2 proposed). No dimension lines show clearance distances from transformer pads to fire hydrants. The 5-foot minimum clearance from fire hydrants cannot be verified from submitted evidence.
applicableAreas: fire hydrant locations on site

findings.comment: Fire hydrant location and transformer pad location are identified but clearance distance is not dimensioned. Provide dimensioned plan showing minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pad edges to fire hydrant structure.
applicableAreas: east-central transformer pad area between Buildings 4, 5, and 7

findings.comment: Landscape Plan shows plantings and shrubs around the site. No dimension lines measure clearance distances from transformer pads to shrubs or low-lying vegetation. The 10-foot clearance from the access door side and 5-foot clearance from other sides cannot be verified. Additionally, transformer pad access door orientation is not identified.
applicableAreas: landscaped areas adjacent to transformer pads

findings.comment: Landscape plan shows vegetation areas but does not dimension shrub and low-lying vegetation clearances to transformer pads. Applicant must provide: (1) equipment detail sheets showing access door orientation on each transformer pad; (2) dimensioned landscape plan showing minimum 10-foot clearance from access door side and minimum 5-foot clearance from other sides to all proposed shrubs and low-lying vegetation.
applicableAreas: landscaping areas adjacent to transformer pads

findings.comment: Landscape Plan shows proposed trees and plantings. No dimension lines measure distances from trees to transformer pad locations or underground electric equipment. No root barrier details or specifications are shown on landscape or detail sheets. If trees are located within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment, required root barrier specifications (4 feet deep, 5 feet from equipment) cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: areas with trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment

findings.comment: No root barrier details are shown on landscape or construction detail sheets. Applicant must provide root barrier detail sheets showing minimum 4-foot depth and 5-foot offset from underground electrical equipment for all trees within 20 lateral feet of transformer pads and underground electrical routing.
applicableAreas: trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electrical equipment

findings.comment: Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations but does not clearly identify all light pole locations or show dimension lines measuring distances between light poles and transformer pads. The 5-foot minimum clearance from light poles cannot be verified from available evidence.
applicableAreas: site areas with light poles and transformer pads

findings.comment: Light pole locations are not specifically dimensioned relative to transformer pads on the site plan. Applicant must provide photometric plan or lighting detail sheets showing all light pole locations and dimensions demonstrating minimum 5-foot clearance to transformer pad edges.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Fire Protection Plan shows fire lanes with dimensions, but no dimension lines measure distances from transformer pad locations to the fire lane boundaries. The 15-foot minimum clearance from fire lanes cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: fire lanes

findings.comment: Fire lanes are not specifically delineated or dimensioned on the fire protection plan relative to transformer pad locations. Applicant must identify which internal driveways are designated fire lanes and provide dimensioned plan showing minimum 15-foot clearance from transformer pad edges to fire lane boundaries.
applicableAreas: all transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Sheet 21 shows four transformer pads, but no dimension lines measure distances between any pair of pads. The 5-foot minimum clearance between transformer pads cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: all transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Four transformer pads are shown on the electrical plan but no clearance dimensions are provided between any of them. Applicant must provide dimensioned plan showing minimum 5-foot clearance between each transformer pad pair.
applicableAreas: all transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations but does not indicate whether gas infrastructure is present on the site or near transformer pads. Gas pressure specifications are not provided. No dimension lines show clearance distances between transformer pads and gas lines. The 24-inch minimum for low-pressure gas and 36-inch minimum for high-pressure gas (60 psi and over) cannot be verified without gas line identification and pressure confirmation.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations (only if gas service is present)

findings.comment: Grading and utility plans show gas infrastructure on the site but the horizontal clearance distances between transformer pads and gas lines are not dimensioned. The required minimum clearance (24 inches for low-pressure, 36 inches for high-pressure) cannot be verified without explicit dimensions or pressure specifications.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations where gas service is present

findings.comment: Site plan shows overhead electric lines labeled 'OHE' along property boundaries, but no transformer pads appear to be located under or directly adjacent to these lines. No 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance dimension lines are shown. If transformer pads are positioned within the 7.5-foot clearance area, this would require verification.
applicableAreas: areas with overhead electric distribution lines (none identified adjacent to transformer pads)

findings.comment: Overhead distribution line locations are not clearly identified on the electrical design plan. The required 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead distribution line conductors cannot be verified. The electrical notes reference consultation with Austin Energy Design regarding overhead lines but overhead line routing is not shown on the submitted plans.
applicableAreas: Transformer locations if overhead distribution conductors are present

findings.comment: Site plan shows overhead electric lines at property boundaries. No dimension lines show distances from transformer pad locations to overhead distribution primary or neutral conductors. The 15-foot radius clearance requirement (measured from conductors) cannot be verified from submitted evidence.
applicableAreas: areas with overhead distribution primary or neutral conductors (none clearly identified adjacent to transformer pads)

findings.comment: Overhead distribution primary and neutral conductor locations are not shown on the submitted electrical plan. The required 15-foot radius clearance (measured from the conductor centerline, not pole centerline) cannot be verified without identifying the specific overhead line locations and conductor positions.
applicableAreas: Transformer locations if overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors are present

findings.comment: Site plan shows property lines and transformer pad locations. No dimension lines or callout notes specifically confirm that all transformer pads are located 100% on private property (not straddling property lines). Plat sheet shows property boundaries, but correlation to transformer pad positions requires explicit callouts not present on electrical plan.
applicableAreas: all transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Property lines are shown on the site and electrical plans, but transformer pad locations are not dimensioned or labeled to explicitly confirm they are 100% located on private property and not straddling property lines. Additionally, facts.md identifies critical undisclosed easements not depicted on the site plan that may affect the property availability for transformer pad installation.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations

findings.comment: No gas pump canopies identified on site plan. Item is not applicable as this is a residential townhome development with no fuel service facilities proposed.
applicableAreas: Site plan - if any gas pump canopies are proposed

findings.comment: Site plan shows driveways and pedestrian walkways but provides no section or plan view exhibits showing 15-foot radial clearance dimensions from overhead electric distribution facilities to the edges of these elevated features or walkways.
applicableAreas: Driveways and pedestrian walkways on site

findings.comment: Driveway posts/barriers may exist near overhead lines, but no section exhibits showing vertical and horizontal clearance verification dimensions from outermost electric line to barrier posts are provided.
applicableAreas: Driveways and site access routes near overhead electric lines on southern property boundary

findings.comment: Site plan shows fire lanes and emergency access routes (Sheet 10) but does not provide section views with clearance dimension annotations from outside conductor of overhead electric facilities showing both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances are maintained for emergency access structures.
applicableAreas: Any emergency access structures or elevated platforms if proposed on site

findings.comment: Vehicle parking areas are proposed on site plan, and overhead electric lines are present. However, no vertical clearance dimension annotations are shown from the lowest point of overhead facilities to parking areas. Code requires compliance with clearance requirements (minimum 12-18 feet depending on use).
applicableAreas: Vehicle parking areas beneath or adjacent to overhead electric lines

findings.comment: Site plan shows fire lanes and potential lighting areas but does not provide photometric plan or explicit streetlight pole locations with clearance verification relative to overhead electric lines.
applicableAreas: Streetlight pole locations relative to overhead electric lines

findings.comment: Site plan shows sidewalk along Valley View Road (western frontage) but does not provide dimension annotations showing sidewalk clearance from existing utility poles at property line. Cannot verify that sidewalk is cleared from poles at each end of property.
applicableAreas: Sidewalk along Valley View Road (western property boundary) where utility poles exist

findings.comment: Preliminary electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows underground service infrastructure but does not show any new power pole locations for underground service conversion or document clearances from new poles to existing poles if applicable.
applicableAreas: Utility plan showing electric service infrastructure conversion from overhead to underground

findings.comment: Photometric plan and landscape plan show site lighting but do not provide clearance verification dimensions from overhead electric lines to decorative or site lighting fixtures showing 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances.
applicableAreas: Decorative lighting fixture locations relative to overhead electric lines

findings.comment: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows utilities and existing features but does not clearly identify or dimension streetlight pole locations adjacent to property with proposed building clearances.
applicableAreas: Buildings relative to existing streetlight poles if any exist on adjacent properties

findings.comment: Preliminary electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer locations on site but does not provide section views with vertical clearance dimensions from overhead electric lines to top of transformer equipment showing 7.5-foot minimum vertical sky-to-ground clearance.
applicableAreas: Transformers and electrical equipment relative to overhead electric lines

findings.comment: Preliminary electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows electrical infrastructure but does not provide building elevation drawings showing service mast locations and roof clearance dimensions (3-foot minimum above roof, or 18-inch if mast within 4 feet of roof edge, for voltages ≤300V).
applicableAreas: Service mast through-roof installations on proposed buildings

findings.comment: Transmission infrastructure referenced in Sheet 3 general notes with stricter 25-foot clearance requirement. Proposed tree species lack UC designation verification per ECM Appendix F. Actual lateral distances from transmission conductors cannot be precisely measured from submitted plans.
applicableAreas: Areas within 50 lateral feet of overhead electric transmission conductors

findings.comment: Mature height per ECM Appendix F cannot be determined from submitted plant specifications. Actual lateral distances from transmission structures cannot be precisely measured. Compliance cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Areas within 50 lateral feet of overhead electric transmission conductors

findings.comment: Site plan shows wooden privacy fences around property perimeter and parking areas. No dimension lines show clearance distances from transformer pads to fence lines. No callouts identify which sides of transformer pads have operators/controls (requiring 5-foot clearance) versus sides without operators/controls (requiring 3-foot clearance). The required fence clearances cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations (only if fences or gates are adjacent)

findings.comment: No clearance dimensions are shown on any sheets. Therefore, it cannot be determined whether reduced 3-foot clearances (to brick/masonry buildings) were proposed, or whether the conditions for the reduction exception (not in confined space, 10 ft+ to windows/doors/ducts, 15 ft+ vertical clearance, 3-hour fire rating) were met. If reduced clearances were intended, evidence of Austin Energy Design written approval is not present in submitted documentation.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations (only if reduced clearances are proposed)

findings.comment: Fire Protection Plan identifies fire exit requirements. No stairwells are explicitly labeled on the site plan as serving fire exits. Dimension lines from transformer pads to any potential stairwell locations are not shown. The 5-foot minimum clearance from stairwells cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations (only if stairwells serving as fire exits are adjacent)

findings.comment: Fire Protection Plan (Sheet 10) shows no fire escapes or stairs serving as fire escapes. No such features appear on the buildings. Requirement to maintain 20-foot clearance from oil-filled equipment is not applicable as the triggering condition (fire escapes/stairs serving as fire exits) is not present.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations (only if fire escapes or stairs serving as fire escapes are present)

findings.comment: Site plan and landscape plan show bicycle parking locations. No dimension lines show clearance distances from transformer pad locations to any bicycle parking areas. The 5-foot minimum clearance requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: parking and common areas (only if bike racks are present)

findings.comment: No cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances inside niches or enclosed transformer access areas were provided. No niche configuration details or 35-foot clearance documentation exists in submitted plans. If any transformer is located in a niche (accessible from outside but within building footprint), this cannot be verified from available evidence.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations (only if located in niche, enclosed area, or notched-out building configuration)

findings.comment: No niche service is identified on submitted plans. No documentation of 3-hour fire wall rating, ventilation specifications, or Austin Energy Design business unit consultation appears in any sheet or supplementary document. If a niche service configuration is proposed, required fire rating and ventilation specifications are not demonstrated.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations (only if located in niche service configuration)

findings.comment: Site plan shows overhead electric lines along property boundaries and transformer locations. No cross-section drawings or vertical clearance documentation confirms that customer structures (buildings, light poles, signs, antennas, tanks) are not installed under Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities. Vertical clearance verification is not provided.
applicableAreas: transformer pad locations and site structures relative to overhead distribution facilities
